description.narrative:
Syftet med inledningsfasen är att utforska och definiera centrala ingångspunkter, frågor och metoder för att stödja allmänintressemedier i att leverera högkvalitativ information och skapa öppna plattformar. Särskild vikt kommer att läggas vid att identifiera de mest effektiva sätten att engagera ungdommar, kvinnor och andra marginaliserade grupper. Under den fyra månader långa inlednings- och samskapandefasen har projektet två huvudmål:
Mål 1: Undersöka, utveckla och definiera prioriterade områden och ingångspunkter inom mediesektorn för att stärka demokratiska processer, ungas deltagande, ansvarstagande och transparens.
Mål 2: Upprätthålla väsentliga medieplattformar och en bredare "infrastruktur" som om gör det möjligt för unga att utkräva ansvar från ledare, samt bevara nödvändiga mekanismer för att skydda pressfriheten och yttrandefriheten.

The purpose of the inception phase is to research, explore, and define key entry points, issues, and approaches to support public interest media in delivering high-quality information and creating open platforms. A particular focus will be on identifying the best ways to engage young people, women and other marginalised groups. For the 4 month inception/co-creation phase, the project features two key objectives:
Objective 1: Research, develop and define key priority areas, and entry points for the media sector for strengthening democratic processes, youth participation, accountability and transparency.
Objective 2: Maintain critical media platforms and wider “infrastructure” for youth to hold leaders accountable and maintain essential mechanisms for the protection of press and freedom of expression.

sector.narrative: Media and free flow of information

description.narrative:
With a focus on research, capacity building, media production of weekly discussion programmes, investigations and social media content, as well as stakeholder engagement and advocacy, this phase aimed to lay the foundational groundwork for the Funsani project, a multi-stakeholder, youth-centred programme and legal reforms that would support better democratic participation, promote accountability, and protect press freedom.
Objective 1: Research, develop and define key priority areas and entry points for the media sector for strengthening democratic processes, youth participation, accountability and transparency
Objective 1 was largely achieved, with the inception phase generating a strong evidence base to guide future programming. Five research studies were completed, offering practical insights into media literacy, youth participation, and journalism practice within the legal environment for press freedom. These findings directly informed tools such as a legal guide for journalists, youth civic engagement resources, and policy submissions. Media literacy data is now shaping the projects communication strategy, while studies on journalism unions and misinformation showed gaps that future interventions will address. The period also saw the successful onboarding of the MISA board, the registration and operationalisation of the Media Self-Regulation Council of Zambia, and the rollout of youth-led accountability boards and a pilot community tracking tool.
Objective 2: Maintain critical media platforms and wider infrastructure for youth to hold leaders accountable and maintain essential mechanisms for the protection of press and freedom of expression
Objective 2 was largely achieved, with clear and measurable progress across multiple areas. The Media Legal Defence Fund directly supported 12 journalists and media houses facing legal threats, including a landmark case that restored a journalists employment after unlawful dismissal. Media monitoring intensified, resulting in a media violations report and plans for a digital dashboard. Policy advocacy led to a presidential statement in support of media self-regulation, while civil society coordination produced concrete legal recommendations shared with Parliament. At the community level, over 900 young people were engaged in civic awareness activities, and municipal councils committed to new transparency measures following youth-led advocacy. In the media space, 144 radio programmes were produced exceeding targets with improved formats and new digital outreach tools and approaches introduced to reach younger audiences more effectively.
